rule: A News Observation belongs to the UTC day in which its qualifying information state is observed in the monitored news flow. The underlying real-world event may have occurred earlier.
rationale: 600 STATES interprets the emotional state of the world's observed news/information flow. An event cannot contribute to the observed state until information about it is present in that flow.

inclusion.timestamp_basis: qualifying MentionTimeDate / independently verified publication or observation timestamp

constraints: An old event merely reprinted without a materially qualifying information state is not automatically a new observation.
Duplicate reporting of the same information state remains one News Observation.
Materially distinct developments within an Event Cluster may qualify as separate News Observations.
The timestamp must be auditable; it may not be inferred for aesthetic or chronological convenience.
Selection is frozen before emotion classification.
Color Protocol v0.4 remains inaccessible until the final 600-observation manifest is frozen.
